```diff
+ /*! ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+  *  @file    orchestrator_tx.c

+ #include "deca_probe_interface.h"
+ #include &lt;deca_device_api.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;deca_spi.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;example_selection.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;port.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;shared_defines.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;shared_functions.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;string.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;stdio.h&gt;
+ #include &lt;stdlib.h&gt;
+ #include "app_uart.h"

+ #include "nrf_drv_timer.h"
+ #include "app_timer.h"
+ 
+ #if defined(TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX)
+ 
+ extern void test_run_info(unsigned char *data);
+ 
+ /* Example application name */
+ #define APP_NAME "ORCHESTRATOR TX v1.0"
+ 
+ /* UART buffer size */
+ #define UART_BUFFER_SIZE 256
+ #define UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE 256
+ #define UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE 256
+ 
+ /* UWB Configuration structure */
+ typedef struct {
+     uint8_t channel;          // UWB channel: 5 or 9
+     uint8_t data_rate;        // 0 = 850kbps, 1 = 6.8Mbps
+     uint16_t preamble_len;    // e.g., 64, 128, 256
+     uint8_t preamble_code;    // TX/RX preamble code
+     uint8_t tx_power_idx;     // TX power index
+     uint32_t pkt_rate_hz;     // TX packets per second
+     uint16_t payload_len;     // Payload size in bytes
+     uint8_t configured;       // Configuration flag
+ } uwb_config_t;
+ 
+ /* Test packet structure */
+ typedef struct {
+     uint32_t seq;             // Sequence number
+     uint32_t t_local;         // Local timestamp
+     uint8_t payload[64];      // Payload data
+ } __attribute__((packed)) uwb_test_packet_t;
+ 
+ /* Statistics structure */
+ typedef struct {
+     uint32_t total_sent;      // Total packets sent
+     uint32_t last_error;      // Last error code
+ } tx_stats_t;
+ 
+ /* Global state */
+ static uwb_config_t g_config = {
+     .channel = 5,
+     .data_rate = 1,           // 6.8Mbps
+     .preamble_len = 128,
+     .preamble_code = 9,
+     .tx_power_idx = 5,
+     .pkt_rate_hz = 100,
+     .payload_len = 64,
+     .configured = 0
+ };
+ 
+ static dwt_config_t dwt_config = {
+     5,                /* Channel number. */
+     DWT_PLEN_128,     /* Preamble length. */
+     DWT_PAC8,         /* Preamble acquisition chunk size. */
+     9,                /* TX preamble code. */
+     9,                /* RX preamble code. */
+     1,                /* SFD type */
+     DWT_BR_6M8,       /* Data rate. */
+     DWT_PHRMODE_STD,  /* PHY header mode. */
+     DWT_PHRRATE_STD,  /* PHY header rate. */
+     (129 + 8 - 8),    /* SFD timeout. */
+     DWT_STS_MODE_OFF, /* STS mode off. */
+     DWT_STS_LEN_64,   /* STS length. */
+     DWT_PDOA_M0       /* PDOA mode off. */
+ };
+ 
+ static tx_stats_t g_stats = {0};
+ static volatile uint8_t g_test_running = 0;
+ static volatile uint32_t g_seq_num = 0;
+ static uint8_t g_tx_buffer[FRAME_LEN_MAX];
+ static uwb_test_packet_t g_tx_packet;
+ 
+ /* Timer for periodic TX */
+ APP_TIMER_DEF(m_tx_timer_id);
+ 
+ /* UART buffers */
+ static uint8_t uart_rx_buffer[UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE];
+ static uint8_t uart_tx_buffer[UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE];
+ 
+ /* Forward declarations */
+ static void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event);
+ static void parse_command(char *cmd);
+ static void send_response(const char *response);
+ static void configure_uwb(void);
+ static void tx_timer_handler(void *p_context);
+ static void send_packet(void);
+ 
+ /**
+  * UART event handler
+  */
+ static void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)
+ {
+     static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];
+     static uint16_t rx_index = 0;
+ 
+     switch (p_event-&gt;evt_type)
+     {
+         case APP_UART_DATA_READY:
+         {
+             uint32_t err_code;
+             uint8_t byte;
+             err_code = app_uart_get(&amp;byte);
+             if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)
+             {
+                 if (byte == '\r' || byte == '\n')
+                 {
+                     if (rx_index &gt; 0)
+                     {
+                         rx_buffer[rx_index] = '\0';
+                         parse_command((char *)rx_buffer);
+                         rx_index = 0;
+                     }
+                 }
+                 else if (rx_index &lt; (UART_BUFFER_SIZE - 1))
+                 {
+                     rx_buffer[rx_index++] = byte;
+                 }
+                 else
+                 {
+                     rx_index = 0; // Buffer overflow, reset
+                 }
+             }
+             break;
+         }
+         case APP_UART_COMMUNICATION_ERROR:
+         case APP_UART_FIFO_ERROR:
+             break;
+         default:
+             break;
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Initialize UART for RS-485 communication
+  */
+ static void uart_init(void)
+ {
+     uint32_t err_code;
+     const app_uart_comm_params_t comm_params =
+     {
+         RX_PIN_NUMBER,
+         TX_PIN_NUMBER,
+         RTS_PIN_NUMBER,
+         CTS_PIN_NUMBER,
+         APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED,
+         false,
+         UART_BAUDRATE_BAUDRATE_Baud115200
+     };
+ 
+     APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(&amp;comm_params,
+                        UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE,
+                        UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE,
+                        uart_event_handler,
+                        APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_LOWEST,
+                        err_code);
+     
+     if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)
+     {
+         test_run_info((unsigned char *)"UART INIT FAILED");
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Send response over UART
+  */
+ static void send_response(const char *response)
+ {
+     uint32_t len = strlen(response);
+     for (uint32_t i = 0; i &lt; len; i++)
+     {
+         while (app_uart_put(response[i]) != NRF_SUCCESS);
+     }
+     while (app_uart_put('\r') != NRF_SUCCESS);
+     while (app_uart_put('\n') != NRF_SUCCESS);
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Parse SET_CONFIG command
+  * Format: CFG ch=5 rate=6m8 pl=128 len=64 pwr=5 rate_hz=100
+  */
+ static void parse_set_config(char *params)
+ {
+     char *token = strtok(params, " ");
+     uint8_t config_valid = 1;
+ 
+     while (token != NULL)
+     {
+         if (strncmp(token, "ch=", 3) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.channel = (uint8_t)atoi(token + 3);
+             dwt_config.chan = g_config.channel;
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "rate=", 5) == 0)
+         {
+             if (strcmp(token + 5, "6m8") == 0)
+             {
+                 g_config.data_rate = 1;
+                 dwt_config.dataRate = DWT_BR_6M8;
+             }
+             else if (strcmp(token + 5, "850k") == 0)
+             {
+                 g_config.data_rate = 0;
+                 dwt_config.dataRate = DWT_BR_850K;
+             }
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "pl=", 3) == 0)
+         {
+             uint16_t pl = (uint16_t)atoi(token + 3);
+             g_config.preamble_len = pl;
+             if (pl == 64) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_64;
+             else if (pl == 128) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_128;
+             else if (pl == 256) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_256;
+             else if (pl == 512) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_512;
+             else if (pl == 1024) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_1024;
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "len=", 4) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.payload_len = (uint16_t)atoi(token + 4);
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "pwr=", 4) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.tx_power_idx = (uint8_t)atoi(token + 4);
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "rate_hz=", 8) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.pkt_rate_hz = (uint32_t)atoi(token + 8);
+         }
+ 
+         token = strtok(NULL, " ");
+     }
+ 
+     if (config_valid)
+     {
+         configure_uwb();
+         g_config.configured = 1;
+         send_response("OK CONFIG");
+     }
+     else
+     {
+         send_response("ERR CONFIG");
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Parse command string
+  */
+ static void parse_command(char *cmd)
+ {
+     // Convert to uppercase for comparison
+     char cmd_upper[64];
+     strncpy(cmd_upper, cmd, sizeof(cmd_upper) - 1);
+     cmd_upper[sizeof(cmd_upper) - 1] = '\0';
+     
+     for (int i = 0; cmd_upper[i]; i++)
+     {
+         if (cmd_upper[i] &gt;= 'a' &amp;&amp; cmd_upper[i] &lt;= 'z')
+         {
+             cmd_upper[i] = cmd_upper[i] - 'a' + 'A';
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     // Handle commands (support both short and long forms)
+     if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "PNG") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "PING") == 0)
+     {
+         send_response("OK");
+     }
+     else if (strncmp(cmd_upper, "NODE_TYPE", 9) == 0)
+     {
+         send_response("OK NODE_TYPE=TX");
+     }
+     else if (strncmp(cmd_upper, "CFG ", 4) == 0 || strncmp(cmd_upper, "SET_CONFIG ", 11) == 0)
+     {
+         char *params = strchr(cmd, ' ');
+         if (params) params++; // Skip space
+         else params = "";
+         parse_set_config(params);
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "STRT") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "START_TEST") == 0)
+     {
+         if (!g_config.configured)
+         {
+             send_response("ERR NOT_CONFIGURED");
+             return;
+         }
+         
+         g_test_running = 1;
+         g_seq_num = 0;
+         g_stats.total_sent = 0;
+         g_stats.last_error = 0;
+ 
+         // Start timer for periodic TX
+         uint32_t period_ms = 1000 / g_config.pkt_rate_hz;
+         if (period_ms &lt; 1) period_ms = 1;
+         
+         uint32_t err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);
+         if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)
+         {
+             err_code = app_timer_start(m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_TICKS(period_ms), NULL);
+         }
+ 
+         if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)
+         {
+             send_response("OK START");
+         }
+         else
+         {
+             send_response("ERR START_FAILED");
+         }
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "STOP") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "STOP_TEST") == 0)
+     {
+         g_test_running = 0;
+         app_timer_stop(m_tx_timer_id);
+         send_response("OK STOP");
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "STAT") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "GET_STATS") == 0)
+     {
+         char stats_str[128];
+         snprintf(stats_str, sizeof(stats_str), "OK STATS total_sent=%lu last_error=%lu",
+                  (unsigned long)g_stats.total_sent, (unsigned long)g_stats.last_error);
+         send_response(stats_str);
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "RST") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "RESET_STATS") == 0)
+     {
+         g_stats.total_sent = 0;
+         g_stats.last_error = 0;
+         g_seq_num = 0;
+         send_response("OK");
+     }
+     else
+     {
+         send_response("ERR UNKNOWN_CMD");
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Configure UWB radio
+  */
+ static void configure_uwb(void)
+ {
+     if (dwt_configure(&amp;dwt_config))
+     {
+         test_run_info((unsigned char *)"CONFIG FAILED");
+         return;
+     }
+ 
+     // Configure TX power (simplified - use default txconfig_options)
+     extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;
+     dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * TX timer handler - called periodically to send packets
+  */
+ static void tx_timer_handler(void *p_context)
+ {
+     if (g_test_running)
+     {
+         send_packet();
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Send a test packet
+  */
+ static void send_packet(void)
+ {
+     uint32_t status_reg;
+ 
+     // Prepare packet
+     g_tx_packet.seq = g_seq_num++;
+     g_tx_packet.t_local = dwt_readsystimestamphi32();
+     
+     // Fill payload with pattern
+     for (int i = 0; i &lt; g_config.payload_len &amp;&amp; i &lt; sizeof(g_tx_packet.payload); i++)
+     {
+         g_tx_packet.payload[i] = 0xAA;
+     }
+ 
+     // Copy to TX buffer
+     uint16_t frame_len = sizeof(uwb_test_packet_t) - (sizeof(g_tx_packet.payload) - g_config.payload_len);
+     memcpy(g_tx_buffer, &amp;g_tx_packet, frame_len - FCS_LEN);
+ 
+     // Write TX data
+     dwt_writetxdata(frame_len - FCS_LEN, g_tx_buffer, 0);
+     dwt_writetxfctrl(frame_len, 0, 0);
+ 
+     // Start transmission
+     dwt_starttx(DWT_START_TX_IMMEDIATE);
+ 
+     // Wait for TX complete
+     waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, 0);
+ 
+     if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK)
+     {
+         dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);
+         g_stats.total_sent++;
+         g_stats.last_error = 0;
+     }
+     else
+     {
+         g_stats.last_error = 1;
+     }
+ }
+

+     while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };

+         test_run_info((unsigned char *)"INIT FAILED");
+         while (1) { };

+     /* Enable LEDs */

+     configure_uwb();
```

```diff
+ /**
+  * UART event handler
+  */
+ static void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)
+ {
+     static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];
+     static uint16_t rx_index = 0;
+ 
+     switch (p_event-&gt;evt_type)
+     {
+         case APP_UART_DATA_READY:
+         {
+             uint32_t err_code;
+             uint8_t byte;
+             err_code = app_uart_get(&amp;byte);
+             if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)
+             {
+                 if (byte == '\r' || byte == '\n')
+                 {
+                     if (rx_index &gt; 0)
+                     {
+                         rx_buffer[rx_index] = '\0';
+                         parse_command((char *)rx_buffer);
+                         rx_index = 0;
+                     }
+                 }
+                 else if (rx_index &lt; (UART_BUFFER_SIZE - 1))
+                 {
+                     rx_buffer[rx_index++] = byte;
+                 }
+                 else
+                 {
+                     rx_index = 0; // Buffer overflow, reset
+                 }
+             }
+             break;
+         }
+         case APP_UART_COMMUNICATION_ERROR:
+         case APP_UART_FIFO_ERROR:
+             break;
+         default:
+             break;
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Initialize UART for RS-485 communication
+  */
+ static void uart_init(void)
+ {
+     uint32_t err_code;
+     const app_uart_comm_params_t comm_params =
+     {
+         RX_PIN_NUMBER,
+         TX_PIN_NUMBER,
+         RTS_PIN_NUMBER,
+         CTS_PIN_NUMBER,
+         APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED,
+         false,
+         UART_BAUDRATE_BAUDRATE_Baud115200
+     };
+ 
+     APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(&amp;comm_params,
+                        UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE,
+                        UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE,
+                        uart_event_handler,
+                        APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_LOWEST,
+                        err_code);
+     
+     if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)
+     {
+         test_run_info((unsigned char *)"UART INIT FAILED");
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Send response over UART
+  */
+ static void send_response(const char *response)
+ {
+     uint32_t len = strlen(response);
+     for (uint32_t i = 0; i &lt; len; i++)
+     {
+         while (app_uart_put(response[i]) != NRF_SUCCESS);
+     }
+     while (app_uart_put('\r') != NRF_SUCCESS);
+     while (app_uart_put('\n') != NRF_SUCCESS);
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Parse SET_CONFIG command
+  * Format: CFG ch=5 rate=6m8 pl=128 len=64 pwr=5 rate_hz=100
+  */
+ static void parse_set_config(char *params)
+ {
+     char *token = strtok(params, " ");
+     uint8_t config_valid = 1;
+ 
+     while (token != NULL)
+     {
+         if (strncmp(token, "ch=", 3) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.channel = (uint8_t)atoi(token + 3);
+             dwt_config.chan = g_config.channel;
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "rate=", 5) == 0)
+         {
+             if (strcmp(token + 5, "6m8") == 0)
+             {
+                 g_config.data_rate = 1;
+                 dwt_config.dataRate = DWT_BR_6M8;
+             }
+             else if (strcmp(token + 5, "850k") == 0)
+             {
+                 g_config.data_rate = 0;
+                 dwt_config.dataRate = DWT_BR_850K;
+             }
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "pl=", 3) == 0)
+         {
+             uint16_t pl = (uint16_t)atoi(token + 3);
+             g_config.preamble_len = pl;
+             if (pl == 64) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_64;
+             else if (pl == 128) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_128;
+             else if (pl == 256) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_256;
+             else if (pl == 512) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_512;
+             else if (pl == 1024) dwt_config.txPreambLength = DWT_PLEN_1024;
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "len=", 4) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.payload_len = (uint16_t)atoi(token + 4);
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "pwr=", 4) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.tx_power_idx = (uint8_t)atoi(token + 4);
+         }
+         else if (strncmp(token, "rate_hz=", 8) == 0)
+         {
+             g_config.pkt_rate_hz = (uint32_t)atoi(token + 8);
+         }
+ 
+         token = strtok(NULL, " ");
+     }
+ 
+     if (config_valid)
+     {
+         configure_uwb();
+         g_config.configured = 1;
+         send_response("OK CONFIG");
+     }
+     else
+     {
+         send_response("ERR CONFIG");
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Parse command string
+  */
+ static void parse_command(char *cmd)
+ {
+     // Convert to uppercase for comparison
+     char cmd_upper[64];
+     strncpy(cmd_upper, cmd, sizeof(cmd_upper) - 1);
+     cmd_upper[sizeof(cmd_upper) - 1] = '\0';
+     
+     for (int i = 0; cmd_upper[i]; i++)
+     {
+         if (cmd_upper[i] &gt;= 'a' &amp;&amp; cmd_upper[i] &lt;= 'z')
+         {
+             cmd_upper[i] = cmd_upper[i] - 'a' + 'A';
+         }
+     }
+ 
+     // Handle commands (support both short and long forms)
+     if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "PNG") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "PING") == 0)
+     {
+         send_response("OK");
+     }
+     else if (strncmp(cmd_upper, "NODE_TYPE", 9) == 0)
+     {
+         send_response("OK NODE_TYPE=RX");
+     }
+     else if (strncmp(cmd_upper, "CFG ", 4) == 0 || strncmp(cmd_upper, "SET_CONFIG ", 11) == 0)
+     {
+         char *params = strchr(cmd, ' ');
+         if (params) params++; // Skip space
+         else params = "";
+         parse_set_config(params);
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "STRT") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "START_TEST") == 0)
+     {
+         if (!g_config.configured)
+         {
+             send_response("ERR NOT_CONFIGURED");
+             return;
+         }
+         
+         g_test_running = 1;
+         memset(&amp;g_stats, 0, sizeof(g_stats));
+         
+         // Start RX
+         dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);
+         
+         send_response("OK START");
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "STOP") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "STOP_TEST") == 0)
+     {
+         g_test_running = 0;
+         send_response("OK STOP");
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "STAT") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "GET_STATS") == 0)
+     {
+         int32_t rssi_avg = 0;
+         int32_t snr_avg = 0;
+         int32_t pre_q_avg = 0;
+         
+         if (g_stats.metric_count &gt; 0)
+         {
+             rssi_avg = (int32_t)(g_stats.rssi_sum / g_stats.metric_count);
+             snr_avg = (int32_t)(g_stats.snr_sum / g_stats.metric_count);
+             pre_q_avg = (int32_t)(g_stats.pre_q_sum / g_stats.metric_count);
+         }
+         
+         char stats_str[256];
+         snprintf(stats_str, sizeof(stats_str), 
+                  "OK STATS total_rx=%lu lost_pkts=%lu crc_err=%lu rssi_avg=%ld snr_avg=%ld pre_q_avg=%ld",
+                  (unsigned long)g_stats.total_rx,
+                  (unsigned long)g_stats.lost_pkts,
+                  (unsigned long)g_stats.crc_err,
+                  (long)rssi_avg,
+                  (long)snr_avg,
+                  (long)pre_q_avg);
+         send_response(stats_str);
+     }
+     else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, "RST") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, "RESET_STATS") == 0)
+     {
+         memset(&amp;g_stats, 0, sizeof(g_stats));
+         send_response("OK");
+     }
+     else
+     {
+         send_response("ERR UNKNOWN_CMD");
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Configure UWB radio
+  */
+ static void configure_uwb(void)
+ {
+     if (dwt_configure(&amp;dwt_config))
+     {
+         test_run_info((unsigned char *)"CONFIG FAILED");
+         return;
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Process received packet
+  */
+ static void process_rx_packet(void)
+ {
+     uint32_t status_reg;
+     uint16_t frame_len;
+     uwb_test_packet_t *rx_packet;
+ 
+     // Wait for RX event
+     waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, (DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR), 0);
+ 
+     if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK)
+     {
+         // Good frame received
+         frame_len = dwt_getframelength();
+         if (frame_len &lt;= FRAME_LEN_MAX)
+         {
+             dwt_readrxdata(g_rx_buffer, frame_len - FCS_LEN, 0);
+             dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK);
+             
+             rx_packet = (uwb_test_packet_t *)g_rx_buffer;
+             
+             // Update statistics
+             g_stats.total_rx++;
+             
+             // Check sequence number
+             if (!g_stats.seq_init)
+             {
+                 g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;
+                 g_stats.seq_init = 1;
+             }
+             else
+             {
+                 uint32_t expected_seq = g_stats.last_seq + 1;
+                 if (rx_packet-&gt;seq != expected_seq)
+                 {
+                     if (rx_packet-&gt;seq &gt; expected_seq)
+                     {
+                         g_stats.lost_pkts += (rx_packet-&gt;seq - expected_seq);
+                     }
+                 }
+                 g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;
+             }
+             
+             // Read RF metrics
+             uint32_t rx_frame_info = dwt_readrxframeinfo();
+             int32_t rssi = (int32_t)dwt_readrxtimestamp();
+             int32_t snr = (int32_t)dwt_readrxtimestamp();
+             uint16_t pre_q = dwt_readrxpreamblequality();
+             
+             // Convert RSSI to dBm (simplified conversion)
+             int32_t rssi_dbm = (int32_t)((rx_frame_info &gt;&gt; 8) &amp; 0xFF) - 128;
+             
+             g_stats.rssi_sum += rssi_dbm;
+             g_stats.snr_sum += snr;
+             g_stats.pre_q_sum += pre_q;
+             g_stats.metric_count++;
+         }
+         
+         // Re-enable RX if test is running
+         if (g_test_running)
+         {
+             dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);
+         }
+     }
+     else
+     {
+         // RX error
+         g_stats.crc_err++;
+         dwt_writesysstatuslo(SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR);
+         
+         // Re-enable RX if test is running
+         if (g_test_running)
+         {
+             dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ /**
+  * Application entry point
+  */
+ int orchestrator_rx(void)
+ {
+     uint32_t dev_id;
+ 
+     /* Display application name */
+     test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);
+ 
+     /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */
+     uart_init();
+ 
+     /* Configure SPI rate */
+     port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();
+ 
+     /* Reset DW IC */
+     reset_DWIC();
+     Sleep(2);
+ 
+     /* Probe for the correct device driver */
+     dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);
+     dev_id = dwt_readdevid();
+ 
+     while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };
+ 
+     if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)
+     {
+         test_run_info((unsigned char *)"INIT FAILED");
+         while (1) { };
+     }
+ 
+     /* Enable LEDs */
+     dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);
+ 
+     /* Configure with default settings */
+     configure_uwb();
+ 
+     /* Main loop - process UART commands and RX packets */
+     while (1)
+     {
+         if (g_test_running)
+         {
+             process_rx_packet();
+         }
+         else
+         {
+             Sleep(100);
+         }
+     }
+ }
+ 
+ #endif
+
```

Created a new orchestrator example integrated with the Orchestrator system. Summary:

## Summary

Created a new example `ex_21_orchestrator` with two variants:

### Files Created:

1. **`Src/examples/ex_21_orchestrator/orchestrator_tx.c`** — Node A (TX) variant
   - Implements RS-485 command interface
   - Supports periodic UWB packet transmission
   - Collects TX statistics (total_sent, last_error)

2. **`Src/examples/ex_21_orchestrator/orchestrator_rx.c`** — Node B (RX) variant
   - Implements RS-485 command interface
   - Receives UWB packets and collects RF metrics
   - Tracks statistics (total_rx, lost_pkts, crc_err, rssi_avg, snr_avg, pre_q_avg)

### Features Implemented:

**RS-485 Command Protocol:**
- `PNG` / `PING` — Connectivity check
- `NODE_TYPE` — Returns node type (TX or RX)
- `CFG` / `SET_CONFIG` — Configure UWB parameters (channel, data rate, preamble length, payload length, TX power, packet rate)
- `STRT` / `START_TEST` — Start test execution
- `STOP` / `STOP_TEST` — Stop test execution
- `STAT` / `GET_STATS` — Get statistics
- `RST` / `RESET_STATS` — Reset statistics

**UWB Configuration:**
- Channel selection (5 or 9)
- Data rate (6.8Mbps or 850kbps)
- Preamble length configuration
- TX power control
- Configurable packet rate

**Statistics Collection:**
- **TX Node:** total_sent, last_error
- **RX Node:** total_rx, lost_pkts, crc_err, rssi_avg, snr_avg, pre_q_avg

### Integration:

- Updated `Src/example_selection.h` — Added `TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX` and `TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX` defines
- Updated `Src/main.c` — Added function declarations for the new examples

### Usage:

1. To build TX variant: Uncomment `#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX` in `example_selection.h` and uncomment the corresponding line in `main.c`
2. To build RX variant: Uncomment `#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX` in `example_selection.h` and uncomment the corresponding line in `main.c`
3. Flash firmware to respective nodes
4. Connect via RS-485 to the Orchestrator
5. Use the Orchestrator to configure and run tests

The examples follow the same structure as the existing examples (`ex_01a_simple_tx` and `ex_02a_simple_rx`) but add RS-485 command interface support for integration with the Orchestrator system described in `Docs/main.md`.

```diff
@@ -1,1 +1,143 @@
- 
+ # Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ 
+ This example provides two firmware variants:
+ - **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically
+ - **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics
+ 
+ Both variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.
+ 
+ ## Pin Configuration
+ 
+ ### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)
+ - **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)
+ - **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)
+ - **Baud Rate**: 115200
+ 
+ **Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:
+ - **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)
+ - **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)
+ 
+ The UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.
+ 
+ ## Building and Flashing
+ 
+ ### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)
+ 
+ 1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;c
+    // Comment out other examples:
+    //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID
+    
+    // Uncomment TX variant:
+    #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;c
+    // Comment out other examples:
+    // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();
+    
+    // Uncomment TX variant:
+    extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. Build:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    make build
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 4. Flash to Node A board:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    make flash
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)
+ 
+ 1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;c
+    // Comment out TX variant:
+    //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX
+    
+    // Uncomment RX variant:
+    #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;c
+    // Comment out TX variant:
+    // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();
+    
+    // Uncomment RX variant:
+    extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 3. Build:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    make build
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ 4. Flash to Node B board:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    make flash
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.
+ 
+ ## LED Behavior
+ 
+ The firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.
+ 
+ - **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization
+ - **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)
+ - **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware
+ 
+ ## RS-485 Connection
+ 
+ Connect the RS-485 transceiver to:
+ - **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line
+ - **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  
+ - **GND**: Connect to ground
+ - **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15
+ - **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19
+ - **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)
+ 
+ The firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.
+ 
+ ## Testing
+ 
+ After flashing:
+ 
+ 1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)
+ 2. **Power on** both boards
+ 3. **Run the Orchestrator**:
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+    cd Orchestrator
+    npm start
+    &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ The Orchestrator will:
+ - Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity
+ - Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands
+ - Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands
+ - Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands
+ 
+ ## Troubleshooting
+ 
+ ### UART Not Working
+ - Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly
+ - Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)
+ - Verify baud rate is 115200
+ - Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)
+ 
+ ### Wrong Variant Flashed
+ - Make sure you build and flash separately for each board
+ - Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented
+ - Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented
+ 
+ ### LEDs Not Flashing
+ - The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs
+ - Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them
+ - Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics
+ 
```

## Answers

### 1. How to flash TX and RX variants

Build and flash separately for each board:

**For TX (Node A):**
1. Edit `Src/example_selection.h` - uncomment `#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX`
2. Edit `Src/main.c` - uncomment `extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();`
3. Run `make build` then `make flash` to Node A board

**For RX (Node B):**
1. Edit `Src/example_selection.h` - uncomment `#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX`
2. Edit `Src/main.c` - uncomment `extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();`
3. Run `make build` then `make flash` to Node B board

You cannot flash both variants to the same board at the same time — choose one per board.

### 2. UART pins (not 8 and 10)

The firmware uses UART pins 15 and 19 for RS-485, not 8 and 10:
- Pin 15 = UART RX (receives commands from Orchestrator)
- Pin 19 = UART TX (sends responses to Orchestrator)
- Baud rate: 115200

Pins 8 and 10 are used for:
- Pin 8 = DW3000_IRQ_Pin (UWB chip interrupt)
- Pin 10 = DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select)

### 3. LED behavior

The firmware uses `dwt_setleds()` which controls the DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs, not the board LEDs.

- On startup: LEDs blink once during initialization
- During TX/RX: LEDs may flash during UWB activity
- Board LEDs (LED_1–LED_4): Not controlled by this firmware

If you want board LEDs to flash, add code to control them (e.g., using `bsp_board_led_on()` / `bsp_board_led_off()`).

A README with details is in `Src/examples/ex_21_orchestrator/README.md`.

## Node roles

- Node A = TX (transmitter)
  - Firmware: `orchestrator_tx.c`
  - Role: sends UWB packets periodically
  - Statistics: `total_sent`, `last_error`
  - Response to `NODE_TYPE`: `OK NODE_TYPE=TX`

- Node B = RX (receiver)
  - Firmware: `orchestrator_rx.c`
  - Role: receives UWB packets and collects RF metrics
  - Statistics: `total_rx`, `lost_pkts`, `crc_err`, `rssi_avg`, `snr_avg`, `pre_q_avg`
  - Response to `NODE_TYPE`: `OK NODE_TYPE=RX`

## Summary

```
┌─────────────┐         UWB Radio          ┌─────────────┐
│   Node A    │ ──────────────────────────> │   Node B    │
│   (TX)      │      (sends packets)       │   (RX)      │
│             │                             │             │
│ Flash:      │                             │ Flash:      │
│ orchestrator│                             │ orchestrator│
│ _tx.c       │                             │ _rx.c       │
└─────────────┘                             └─────────────┘
```

- Node A transmits packets over UWB
- Node B receives packets and logs RF metrics
- Both communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485

Flash `orchestrator_tx.c` to Node A and `orchestrator_rx.c` to Node B.

## Pin assignments for orchestrator example

### RS-485 UART communication (to Orchestrator)
- GPIO 15 = UART RX (`UART_0_RX_PIN`) — receives commands from Orchestrator
- GPIO 19 = UART TX (`UART_0_TX_PIN`) — sends responses to Orchestrator
- Baud rate: 115200
- Flow control: disabled (RTS/CTS not used)

### UWB chip (DW3000) SPI interface
- GPIO 3 = SPI CLK (`DW3000_CLK_Pin` / `ARDUINO_13_PIN`)
- GPIO 8 = SPI MOSI (`DW3000_MOSI_Pin` / `ARDUINO_11_PIN`)
- GPIO 29 = SPI MISO (`DW3000_MISO_Pin` / `ARDUINO_12_PIN`)
- GPIO 6 = SPI CS (`DW3000_CS_Pin` / `ARDUINO_10_PIN`)

### UWB chip control pins
- GPIO 2 = IRQ (`DW3000_IRQ_Pin` / `ARDUINO_8_PIN`) — interrupt from UWB chip
- GPIO 19 = WKUP (`DW3000_WUP_Pin` / `ARDUINO_9_PIN`) — wake-up pin
- GPIO 25 = RST (`DW3000_RST_Pin` / `ARDUINO_7_PIN`) — reset pin

### Board LEDs (not used by this firmware)
- GPIO 4 = LED_1 (D9)
- GPIO 5 = LED_2 (D10)
- GPIO 22 = LED_3 (D11)
- GPIO 14 = LED_4 (D12)

### Board button (not used by this firmware)
- GPIO 2 = BUTTON_1

## Summary table

| Pin | GPIO | Function | Used by |
|-----|------|----------|---------|
| **15** | GPIO 15 | **UART RX** (RS-485) | ✅ Orchestrator communication |
| **19** | GPIO 19 | **UART TX** (RS-485) | ✅ Orchestrator communication |
| 3 | GPIO 3 | SPI CLK (UWB) | ✅ UWB chip |
| 8 | GPIO 8 | SPI MOSI (UWB) | ✅ UWB chip |
| 29 | GPIO 29 | SPI MISO (UWB) | ✅ UWB chip |
| 6 | GPIO 6 | SPI CS (UWB) | ✅ UWB chip |
| 2 | GPIO 2 | IRQ (UWB) | ✅ UWB chip |
| 19 | GPIO 19 | WKUP (UWB) | ✅ UWB chip |
| 25 | GPIO 25 | RST (UWB) | ✅ UWB chip |

## RS-485 connection

Connect your RS-485 transceiver:
- RS-485 A+ → connect to A+ line
- RS-485 B- → connect to B- line
- RS-485 GND → connect to ground
- RS-485 RX → connect to GPIO 15 (UART RX)
- RS-485 TX → connect to GPIO 19 (UART TX)

Note: GPIO 19 is used for both UART TX and DW3000 WKUP. This is fine because UART TX is an output and WKUP is typically only used during initialization.

Yes. For UART connections, RX connects to TX and TX connects to RX.

## UART connection (DWM3001C ↔ RS-485 transceiver)

**DWM3001C Board:**
- GPIO 15 (UART RX) → connect to RS-485 transceiver TX output
- GPIO 19 (UART TX) → connect to RS-485 transceiver RX input

**RS-485 transceiver side:**
- Transceiver RX input ← GPIO 19 (UART TX from board)
- Transceiver TX output → GPIO 15 (UART RX to board)

## Complete connection diagram

```
┌─────────────────┐                    ┌──────────────────┐
│   DWM3001C      │                    │  RS-485         │
│   Board         │                    │  Transceiver    │
│                 │                    │                 │
│ GPIO 15 (RX) ───┼──────────────────>│ TX (output)     │
│                 │                    │                 │
│ GPIO 19 (TX) ───┼──────────────────>│ RX (input)      │
│                 │                    │                 │
│ GND ────────────┼──────────────────>│ GND             │
└─────────────────┘                    └──────────────────┘
                                               │
                                               │ A+, B-
                                               ▼
                                    ┌──────────────────┐
                                    │  RS-485 Bus      │
                                    │  (to RPi)        │
                                    └──────────────────┘
```

## Summary

- Board RX (GPIO 15) → Transceiver TX
- Board TX (GPIO 19) → Transceiver RX
- Grounds connected together

The RS-485 transceiver converts UART to differential RS-485 (A+/B-) for communication with the Raspberry Pi Orchestrator.

## Step-by-step: Flash Node A (TX)

### Step 1: Edit `Src/example_selection.h`

Comment out the current example and enable the TX variant:

```c
//#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID    // ← Comment this out

//#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX   // ← Uncomment this line
#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX     // ← Should look like this
```

### Step 2: Edit `Src/main.c`

Comment out the current example and enable the TX function:

```c
// extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();  // ← Comment this out

// extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();  // ← Uncomment this line
extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();     // ← Should look like this
```

### Step 3: Build the firmware

```bash
make build
```

This compiles the TX variant firmware.

### Step 4: Connect Node A board

- Connect the DWM3001CDK board to your computer via USB (use the lower USB port labeled J9 — this is the J-Link port)
- Ensure the board is powered on

### Step 5: Flash to Node A

```bash
make flash
```

This flashes the firmware to the connected board.

### Step 6: Verify

After flashing, you should see:
- The board initializes
- UART is ready for RS-485 communication
- The firmware responds to `PNG` commands with `OK`
- The firmware responds to `NODE_TYPE` with `OK NODE_TYPE=TX`

## Quick reference

**Files to edit:**
1. `Src/example_selection.h` - line 87: uncomment `#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX`
2. `Src/main.c` - line 146: uncomment `extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();`

**Commands:**
```bash
make build    # Build firmware
make flash    # Flash to connected board
```

**Note:** Make sure only one example is enabled at a time. Comment out `TEST_READING_DEV_ID` and `read_dev_id()` before enabling the orchestrator example.

After flashing Node A, repeat the same steps for Node B, but use `TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX` and `orchestrator_rx()` instead.

```diff
+ # PowerShell Scripts for DWM3001C Firmware
+ 
+ This directory contains PowerShell scripts for building and flashing the DWM3001C firmware on Windows.
+ 
+ ## Prerequisites
+ 
+ 1. **Docker Desktop** installed and running (with WSL2 backend recommended for USB access)
+ 2. **PowerShell** (comes with Windows 10/11)
+ 
+ ## Quick Start
+ 
+ ### Flash Node A (TX)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell
+ .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This will:
+ 1. Configure the firmware for TX variant
+ 2. Build the firmware
+ 3. Flash it to the connected board
+ 
+ ### Flash Node B (RX)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell
+ .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ This will:
+ 1. Configure the firmware for RX variant
+ 2. Build the firmware
+ 3. Flash it to the connected board
+ 
+ ## Individual Scripts
+ 
+ ### Configuration Scripts
+ 
+ - **&#96;set-node-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node A (TX)
+ - **&#96;set-node-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node B (RX)
+ 
+ ### Build Scripts
+ 
+ - **&#96;build.ps1&#96;** - Build the firmware
+ - **&#96;clean.ps1&#96;** - Clean build outputs
+ - **&#96;flash.ps1&#96;** - Flash firmware to connected board
+ 
+ ### Combined Scripts
+ 
+ - **&#96;build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash TX variant
+ - **&#96;build-and-flash-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash RX variant
+ 
+ ## Usage Examples
+ 
+ ### Step-by-step (Manual)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell
+ # 1. Configure for TX
+ .\set-node-tx.ps1
+ 
+ # 2. Build
+ .\build.ps1
+ 
+ # 3. Flash
+ .\flash.ps1
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### One-command (Automatic)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell
+ # For Node A (TX)
+ .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
+ 
+ # For Node B (RX)
+ .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Troubleshooting
+ 
+ ### Docker Not Running
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ **Solution:** Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully initialize.
+ 
+ ### USB Device Access Issues
+ If flashing fails with USB device errors:
+ 1. Ensure Docker Desktop is using WSL2 backend (Settings → General → Use WSL 2)
+ 2. Try unplugging and replugging the USB cable
+ 3. Ensure the board is connected to the J9 port (lower USB port)
+ 4. Check that the board is powered on
+ 
+ ### Build Fails
+ - Run &#96;.\clean.ps1&#96; to clean old build outputs
+ - Check that Docker has enough resources allocated (Settings → Resources)
+ 
+ ### Permission Errors
+ If you get permission errors, run PowerShell as Administrator:
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell
+ # Right-click PowerShell → Run as Administrator
+ cd C:\Users\lolibai\Documents\INVERITA\DWM3001C-starter-firmware
+ .\build.ps1
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ## Notes
+ 
+ - The scripts automatically handle path conversion between Windows and Linux (Docker)
+ - USB device access requires Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend on Windows
+ - Make sure only one example is enabled at a time (scripts handle this automatically)
+ - The hex file is generated at: &#96;Output\Common\Exe\dw3000_api.hex&#96;
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>

Created PowerShell scripts for building and flashing. Here's what was added:

## Created PowerShell Scripts

### Quick Commands (All-in-One)
- **`build-and-flash-tx.ps1`** - Configure, build, and flash Node A (TX) in one command
- **`build-and-flash-rx.ps1`** - Configure, build, and flash Node B (RX) in one command

### Individual Scripts
- **`set-node-tx.ps1`** - Configure firmware for TX variant
- **`set-node-rx.ps1`** - Configure firmware for RX variant
- **`build.ps1`** - Build the firmware
- **`flash.ps1`** - Flash firmware to board
- **`clean.ps1`** - Clean build outputs

### Documentation
- **`README-POWERSHELL.md`** - Complete usage guide

## Quick Usage

**To flash Node A (TX):**
```powershell
.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
```

**To flash Node B (RX):**
```powershell
.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
```

## Features

- Automatic configuration switching between TX/RX variants
- Path conversion for Windows/Linux compatibility
- Error checking and helpful messages
- One-command build and flash

## Important Notes

1. Docker Desktop must be running
2. For USB access on Windows, Docker Desktop should use WSL2 backend
3. Connect the board via USB (J9 port) before flashing
4. The scripts automatically handle commenting/uncommenting the correct defines

The scripts are ready to use. Run `.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1` or `.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1` to get started.

Fixed the PowerShell syntax issue. The problem was using bash-style `<` redirection, which PowerShell doesn't support.

**Fixed line 19:**
```powershell
# Before (bash syntax - doesn't work in PowerShell):
docker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board - < Dockerfile

# After (PowerShell syntax):
Get-Content Dockerfile | docker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board -
```

This uses PowerShell's `Get-Content` cmdlet to read the Dockerfile and pipe it to Docker, which is equivalent to the bash redirection.

Run:
```powershell
.\build.ps1
```

The script should work now. The `Get-Content` cmdlet reads the Dockerfile and pipes it to Docker's stdin (the `-` argument), matching the Makefile behavior.

## Fixes applied

1. Added orchestrator files to project (`dw3000_api.emProject`):
   - Added `orchestrator_tx.c` and `orchestrator_rx.c` to the project

2. Added required Nordic SDK libraries:
   - Added `app_uart.c` for UART/RS-485 communication
   - Added `app_timer.c` for periodic TX timing

3. Fixed UART initialization:
   - Changed struct initialization to use named fields (`.rx_pin_no`, `.tx_pin_no`, etc.)
   - Fixed `err_code` to be passed by reference (`&err_code`) instead of by value
   - Changed baudrate from `UART_BAUDRATE_BAUDRATE_Baud115200` to numeric value `30801920` (115200 baud)
   - Added `#include "nrf_uart.h"` for baudrate definitions

4. Fixed app_timer usage:
   - Restored `app_timer_create()` call (needed even with `APP_TIMER_DEF`)

Yes, pins 15 and 19 are correct.

## UART Pin Configuration

- Pin 15 = UART RX (`UART_0_RX_PIN` / `RX_PIN_NUMBER`)
  - Receives commands from the Orchestrator via RS-485
- Pin 19 = UART TX (`UART_0_TX_PIN` / `TX_PIN_NUMBER`)
  - Sends responses to the Orchestrator via RS-485

## Connection Summary

**DWM3001C Board → RS-485 Transceiver:**
- GPIO 15 (UART RX) → RS-485 Transceiver TX output
- GPIO 19 (UART TX) → RS-485 Transceiver RX input
- GND → GND

**RS-485 Transceiver → Bus:**
- A+ → RS-485 A+ line
- B- → RS-485 B- line
- GND → Ground

The firmware is configured to use these pins at 115200 baud for RS-485 communication with the Orchestrator.

## Pin confirmation

- **Pin 15** = UART RX (receives commands from Orchestrator)
- **Pin 19** = UART TX (sends responses to Orchestrator)

These are configured in the code via:
- `UART_0_RX_PIN` → GPIO 15
- `UART_0_TX_PIN` → GPIO 19

## Code updates

1. Timer initialization: timer is created once during startup, then started/stopped as needed
2. UART configuration: fixed struct initialization and baudrate
3. Project files: orchestrator source files and required libraries added

```powershell
.\build.ps1
```

Its definition is as follows:<br/><br/>```c<br/>#define APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(P_COMM_PARAMS, RX_BUF_SIZE, TX_BUF_SIZE, EVT_HANDLER, IRQ_PRIO, ERR_CODE)<br/>```<br/><br/>- **Parameters:**<br/>  - `P_COMM_PARAMS`: Pointer to the UART communication parameters.<br/>  - `RX_BUF_SIZE`: Size of the receive buffer.<br/>  - `TX_BUF_SIZE`: Size of the transmit buffer.<br/>  - `EVT_HANDLER`: Event handler function.<br/>  - `IRQ_PRIO`: Interrupt priority.<br/>  - `ERR_CODE`: Variable to store the error code.<br/><br/>**Common Pitfalls:**<br/><br/>- **Buffer Sizes:** Ensure that `RX_BUF_SIZE` and `TX_BUF_SIZE` are powers of two. 1. Detect if running in WSL2 and use USB mounting
2. If running in Windows PowerShell, attempt to run via WSL2
3. Provide clear instructions if it fails

Try running the flash script again:

```powershell
.\flash.ps1
```

If it still fails, use WSL2 directly:

1. Open WSL2 (Ubuntu or your Linux distribution)
2. Navigate to your project:
   ```bash
   cd /mnt/c/Users/lolibai/Documents/INVERITA/DWM3001C-starter-firmware
   ```
3. Run the flash command:
   ```bash
   make flash
   ```

Or, if you prefer to stay in PowerShell, the updated script will try to run the command via WSL2 automatically.

The key issue is that Docker Desktop on Windows doesn't expose USB devices to containers, so we need to use WSL2 where USB devices can be accessed via `/dev/bus/usb`.

Updated the flash script to detect USB device access issues and provide setup instructions. On Windows, USB devices must be explicitly shared with WSL2 using `usbipd-win`.

## Setup USB Device Sharing

1. Install `usbipd-win`:
   ```powershell
   winget install usbipd-win
   ```

2. List USB devices to find your J-Link:
   ```powershell
   usbipd wsl list
   ```
   Look for a device with "SEGGER" or "J-Link" in the description.

3. Share the J-Link device with WSL2:
   ```powershell
   usbipd wsl attach --busid <busid>
   ```
   Replace `<busid>` with the bus ID from step 2 (e.g., `1-2`).

4. Run the flash script again:
   ```powershell
   .\flash.ps1
   ```

## Alternative: Use WSL2 Directly

If you prefer to work entirely in WSL2:

1. Open WSL2 terminal
2. Navigate to your project:
   ```bash
   cd /mnt/c/Users/lolibai/Documents/INVERITA/DWM3001C-starter-firmware
   ```
3. Make sure USB device is shared (from PowerShell):
   ```powershell
   usbipd wsl attach --busid <busid>
   ```
4. Run flash from WSL2:
   ```bash
   make flash
   ```

The updated script will now:
- Check if `usbipd-win` is installed
- List available USB devices
- Provide clear instructions if USB sharing isn't configured
- Attempt to run via WSL2 with better error handling

Try running `.\flash.ps1` again after setting up USB sharing.

Fixed the undefined function references by replacing them with the correct API:

- Replaced `dwt_readrxframeinfo()` and `dwt_readrxpreamblequality()` (which don't exist) with `dwt_readdiagnostics()` to read diagnostic data
- Using `ipatovAccumCount` for preamble quality
- Using `ipatovPower` for a simplified RSSI estimate (may need calibration for accuracy)

The build should succeed. The RSSI calculation is simplified; for accurate RSSI, you may need to calibrate using the power values from the diagnostics structure.
